Subject: Marketplace listing - residency + deletion controls Qs

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the marketplace walkthrough yesterday. Our security team has a few follow-ups before we finalize the listing and contract:

1) Can Redwood guarantee that data from our customers (end users) will remain in the selected cloud region (US, EU, APAC) when served via the marketplace listing across AWS/GCP/Azure? How is region selection enforced for hosted vs. dedicated vs. private deployments?
2) What are the default retention periods for request logs, prompts, and generated outputs? Can retention be configured per-customer?
3) We need a documented deletion flow: how soon after a deletion request are tokens/outputs purged, what about cached prefix/KV cache, and do you provide attestations?
4) For marketplace listings, what wording can we put in our security docs to describe residency/retention options?

We'd appreciate a short Q&A and any artifacts (matrix, spec) we can share with our procurement and legal teams. Attaching our vendor checklist for reference.

Best,

Subject: Residency enforcement + marketplace wording (draft)

Vanessa / Kim —

Quick draft answers below (happy to refine language for the marketplace asset):

1) Region enforcement (hosted / dedicated / private)- Hosted API: Customers can select a serving region at the account level (US / EU / APAC). For marketplace listings we support region routing via request headers or account configuration. Data residency for hosted is enforced by pinning a model instance and storage to region-specific clusters; routing policy prevents cross-region fallthrough for requests from that account, except for operational fallback which is disabled by default for marketplace listings unless explicitly allowed.

- GCP/AWS/Azure parity: We operate in equivalent regions across the three clouds (e.g., us-west equivalents). Where an exact region doesn't exist, we advertise the nearest region pair (e.g., us-central -> us-west) and document it in the listing matrix.

- Dedicated: With Dedicated, the customer's capacity is provisioned in the selected cloud/region and we provide a region SLA. No cross-region replication of customer inference data.

- Private (VPC/on-prem): Full customer control — all inference traffic and storage remain in the VPC or on-prem environment. Residency is managed by the customer's infra.

2) Retention defaults and per-customer settings- Defaults: request logs (30 days), prompts/outputs (90 days) for hosted accounts.
- Configurable: For marketplace-integrated customers we expose retention configuration at the account level (30/90/180/365 days) and an option for "no retention" where the account opts out of stored prompts/outputs (note: auditing/troubleshooting impact).
- Audit logs: separate audit retention policy (default 365 days, configurable on enterprise tiers).

3) Deletion flow- User request: We support an API-based deletion endpoint and admin console "Erase data" action.
- Timeline: deletion requests trigger background purge jobs; most prompt/output records are irreversibly removed within 24 hours; full KV/prefix cache purge may take up to 72 hours depending on in-flight sessions and cache propagation.
- Evidence: We can provide deletion logs and a timestamped attestation (signed) on request for marketplace customers on dedicated plans. For hosted marketplace customers we provide a deletion confirmation and event ID; for Dedicated/Private we can support a stronger attestation as part of the contract.

4) Marketplace wording (suggestion)- "Redwood Inference supports regionally pinned inference for AWS, GCP, and Azure. Customers may choose a serving region at account provisioning; data processed for inference is stored and served from the selected region. Retention and deletion controls are configurable per account; standard retention is 90 days for prompts/outputs and 30 days for request logs. Dedicated and Private deployments additionally support contractual attestations for deletion and data residency."

Notes / caveats:
- Edge cases: Cross-region fallback (disabled by default in marketplace) and CDN/caching are documented separately.
- Encryption: all data at rest is encrypted with customer KMS options on Dedicated/Private; hosted supports server-side encryption with provider-managed keys or customer-supplied KMS for enterprise customers.

I attached a concise matrix and a short deletion API spec for Kim to verify. Happy to refine language for CloudBridge's procurement doc.

-Karthik
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Residency and deletion controls - confirmations + artifacts

Sara / Vanessa —

Adding a few operational confirmations and the artifacts:

- Retention behavior: When an account opts into "no retention" we stop persisting prompts/outputs to long-term storage; ephemeral caches may still hold short-lived data for active sessions (TTL < 2 minutes).
- Deletion evidence: For marketplace customers we provide a signed confirmation PDF with event ID and timestamps. For Dedicated customers we can append a SOC2-aligned deletion attestation clause in the contract.
- Logs & exports: We can deliver deleted-record logs via S3/GS/Azure Blob export for a one-time delivery within 3 business days when requested by procurement.

Attachments included:
- Redwood_Residency_OnePager.pdf (one-page summary for marketplace listing)
- Marketplace_Residency_Matrix.xlsx (region mapping & fallback rules)
- Deletion_API_Spec.md (endpoint, payloads, sample responses)

If CloudBridge wants standard marketplace copy, I suggest the copy Karthik drafted with two small edits (call out "no cross-region transfer unless customer enables fallback" and "deletion attestation available on Dedicated/Private").

Kimberly Park

Sara —

Attached is a consolidated Q&A, the one-pager for your marketplace listing, and the region matrix. Key points for procurement:

- Residency: Customers choose the serving region at account provisioning; hosted Marketplace accounts are pinned to the chosen region with cross-region fallback disabled by default. Dedicated and Private provide stronger contractual residency guarantees.
- Retention: Default 90 days for prompts/outputs, 30 days for request logs; configurable per account (30/90/180/365 or zero retention opt-out).
- Deletion: API + admin erase action; typical purge within 24-72 hours depending on cache state. Signed deletion attestations available for Dedicated and Private contracts; hosted marketplace customers receive confirmation + event ID.

I've attached the artifacts: Redwood_Residency_OnePager.pdf, Marketplace_Residency_Matrix.xlsx, Deletion_API_Spec.md. Let me know if you'd like a short 30-minute call next week to run procurement through the artifacts — happy to set that up.
